records.title: BackgroundEventLoop.stop() can hang indefinitely during DBOS.destroy()
records.body_excerpt: ## Summary `BackgroundEventLoop.stop()` calls `self._thread.join()` **without a timeout**, which can cause `DBOS.destroy()` to hang indefinitely if any async task in the background event loop doesn't respond to cancellation. This is inconsistent with how the rest of `_destroy()` handles shutdown — background threads are joined with a 10-second timeout (line 716), but the event loop thread has no such protection. ## Reproduction In a long-running server (e.g. FastAPI on Cloud Run), call `DBOS.destroy(workflow_completion_timeout_sec=5)` during shutdown. If any coroutine submitted to the `BackgroundEventLoop` is stuck or doesn't handle `asyncio.CancelledError`, the process hangs

records.title: Enhancement: async-native `recv_async` / `get_event_async` / `sleep_async` to support large concurrent waiter counts
records.body_excerpt: ### What I'd like to see `DBOS.recv_async` (and `get_event_async` / `sleep_async`) currently consume one thread from the DBOS executor pool for the entire duration of the wait, because they're implemented as `asyncio.to_thread(<sync_blocking_fn>)` where the sync function ultimately calls `threading.Condition.wait(timeout=...)` or `time.sleep(...)`.
